quote: Yeah. Alright. Are you open to removing those trees?
stewart_read: This is a design/feasibility judgment call — whether shading disqualifies the roof — that belongs to the specialist's site assessment, not the setter's qualifying call. The rep asserts a visual read ('shade half of your home') and asks the customer to remove trees before any real evaluation.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as legitimate pre-qualification (checking for a hard DQ before booking), but the rep never frames it that way — no mention of a hard shading threshold, just an open-ended design opinion followed by uncertainty ('I'm not too sure').
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the escape hatch: note the trees/roof shape for the specialist's file and move on, rather than debating shading feasibility live with the customer.

quote: What did Sunrun say? I want them to be. I do. It's my home. And then they're gonna put it where I want it and they ain't gonna put nothing.
stewart_read: The customer surfaces friction with someone (likely his daughter) over panel placement and references Sunrun directly, but the rep's response at 07:11 ('What did Sunrun say? Did they say anything about the trees?') only chases the tree angle and never clarifies the placement/ownership dynamic revealed here.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this tangent too confusing to unpack live given the customer's disorganized speech — a reasonable reactive choice, but it leaves competitive and family-dynamic context uncaptured.
coaching_implication: When a customer reveals tension with a co-decider over a competing quote, that's worth a direct clarifying question — the closer needs to know who is actually driving the placement decision.

quote: They didn't give us a a a price or anything. Did they? Yeah. $90 a month.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a live competitor number ($90/month from Sunrun) — a strong anchor for a comparison pitch — but the rep's very next line drops it entirely ('I don't know what you're just telling me. Okay. No worries.') and pivots to the ComEd bill instead of using the number to build curiosity about savings.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the number too ambiguous (lease payment vs. system cost vs. savings) to build on live, choosing to anchor on the verified utility bill instead — a defensible reactive call given the customer's confused delivery.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to at least tag the number for the handoff ('so Sunrun quoted $90/month — got it, I'll flag that for our specialist to beat') rather than visibly waving it off with 'no worries.'

quote: well, I got one here that's $88.79
stewart_read: The customer reads an actual bill number off the paper bill. This is the anchor moment the whole qualifying call is supposed to produce.
coaching_implication: See bill_anchor_audit — the number was captured but never flipped into a savings/pain reframe before the rep moved to scheduling.

quote: Oh, did she send you she sent you a a mench a a picture.
stewart_read: Buried in the same breath the customer mentions 'I gotta go to the Friday, I gotta go to the VA' — a vulnerability disclosure (veteran, medical appointment) that the rep never acknowledges; the rep's next line jumps straight to confirming the daughter's involvement in scheduling.
alternative_hypothesis: The VA reference may simply be a scheduling constraint with no deeper vulnerability intended, making silence a reasonable read rather than a missed empathy beat.
coaching_implication: A one-line acknowledgment ('appreciate your service — we'll work around the VA visit') costs nothing and builds trust; worth flagging as a pattern to watch for, though the stakes here are low since it didn't derail scheduling.

quote: Alright. Great. Thank you for your time, Kevin.
stewart_read: The call ends immediately after the date/time is set with no recap of the appointment, no one-hour block mention, no no-driving/computer instruction, no 'is that fair?' handshake, and no text-followup promise.
alternative_hypothesis: None — the transcript shows no button-up language at all after the time is locked; this is a clear procedural omission, not a strategic compression, given the call had time to spare.
coaching_implication: Drill the full button_up sequence as a closing checklist — recap day/time, hour block, no-driving/computer ask, 'is that fair?', and the text-confirmation promise — every time, regardless of how the scheduling conversation went.

quote: Yeah. Great. We would love to also meet with your daughter. I know, she might be a little hesitant to meet with us. But if she's available, we can show what we're offering to see if it'll fit your needs. What time would work best for you both tomorrow?
stewart_read: The rep correctly identifies the daughter as a co-title-holder (captured earlier at 03:48) and proactively invites her to the appointment — a good protocol-compliant move, matching the adult_child_decision_maker pattern.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example worth reinforcing — the rep remembered the earlier verify answer and looped the co-owner into the booking without treating it as an objection to overcome.
